items.stem: You must look up a price in an unsorted product table and return an exact match. Which is the most reliable choice?

options.rationale: TRUE performs approximate match and needs sorted data; it can return wrong results.
Correct: XLOOKUP defaults to exact match and works on unsorted data.
HLOOKUP searches rows and TRUE is still approximate match.
LOOKUP assumes ascending sorted data and gives unreliable results otherwise.

items.explanation: Correct: XLOOKUP defaults to exact match and works on unsorted data.

items.stem: A colleague saves a budget as an Excel template (.xltx). What happens when they double-click it later?

options.text: It opens a new workbook based on the template
options.rationale: Correct: opening a template creates a new workbook, leaving the template intact.

options.text: It opens and overwrites the template as they edit
options.rationale: Editing a file opened from a template does not overwrite the template itself.
The template remains .xltx; only the new workbook is a normal file.

options.text: It locks the template for all users
options.rationale: Opening a template does not lock it for others.

items.explanation: Correct: opening a template creates a new workbook, leaving the template intact.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about a PivotTable built on an external range? (Select TWO)

options.text: It must be refreshed to reflect new source rows
options.rationale: Correct: a PivotTable caches data and needs a refresh to pick up changes.

options.text: Adding a slicer lets users filter it interactively
options.rationale: Correct: slicers provide interactive filtering of a PivotTable.

options.text: It automatically rewrites the source data
options.rationale: A PivotTable summarizes; it never edits the source.
PivotTables can show subtotals and grand totals.

items.explanation: Correct: a PivotTable caches data and needs a refresh to pick up changes.
